creative_originality.rationale: [NEW_EVIDENCE, Roster32] A second, independent, specific instance beyond his career-spanning stylistic range: on 10 November 1933 at a Buenos Aires banquet honoring both him and Federico García Lorca, the two poets spontaneously delivered a jointly-improvised speech 'al alimón' -- named for a rare bullfighting technique where two matadors work one cape together -- standing simultaneously from opposite ends of the table and alternating lines, corroborated across the Fundación Pablo Neruda's own cultural portal and multiple independent Argentine press retrospectives. Produced work spanning radically different poetic modes across his career — from the surrealist Residencia en la tierra to the accessible political epic Canto General to the intimate Odas Elementales — documented via the well-noted stylistic range across his bibliography.

cross_domain_range.rationale: Sustained parallel careers as a prolific poet and as a career diplomat (consular postings across Asia and Latin America, later senator and ambassador), documented via the well-established dual record of his professional life.

achievement_drive.rationale: Produced an unusually large body of published poetry (dozens of volumes) across a five-decade career while simultaneously sustaining a full diplomatic and political career, documented via his extensive bibliography.

risk_tolerance.rationale: Publicly denounced Chilean president González Videla in a 1948 Senate speech and was subsequently forced into hiding and exile for over a year, escaping Chile on horseback across the Andes — a specific, well-documented instance of real, realized personal risk taken for a political position.

impact_motivation.rationale: Canto General explicitly frames Latin American history and social struggle as its subject, and his sustained political career (Communist Party senator, later ambassador) documents a consistent orientation toward broader social and political purpose alongside his literary work.

social_assertiveness.rationale: Sustained a prominent public political and diplomatic career including elected office and international ambassadorial roles, documented via the well-established record of his public life.

persuasiveness.rationale: His poetry achieved unusually broad popular readership across Latin America and internationally during his own lifetime, documented via the well-established scale of his public reception, distinct from more narrowly literary-audience poets.

discipline.rationale: Sustained an unusually prolific poetic output across five decades while simultaneously maintaining a demanding diplomatic career, evidencing real disciplined effort across two concurrent demanding tracks.

conflict_tolerance.rationale: Sustained direct public political confrontation with the sitting Chilean government leading to his forced exile, documented via the well-established consequences of his own 1948 Senate denunciation.

adaptability.rationale: Sustained productive work through multiple diplomatic postings across very different countries and cultural contexts (Burma, Ceylon, Argentina, Mexico, France) over his career, documented via the well-established record of his consular assignments.

curiosity.rationale: His extensive diplomatic postings across Asia and the Americas and his poetry's engagement with everyday objects (the Odas Elementales) suggest real sustained intellectual and sensory curiosity about the world.

autonomy_need.rationale: Continued pursuing his own political and poetic convictions despite the direct personal cost of exile, suggesting real preference for standing by his own position over institutional accommodation.

resourcefulness.rationale: Escaped Chile on horseback across a mountain pass in the Andes with the help of a clandestine support network during his 1948-49 forced hiding, a specific, well-documented instance of resourceful action under real material and physical constraint.

mastery_orientation.rationale: Continued developing distinct poetic styles across his career (from surrealist to epic-political to intimate-domestic modes) rather than repeating one successful early approach.

leadership_drive.rationale: Held elected political office (Chilean Senate) and later served as a Communist Party presidential pre-candidate before withdrawing in favor of Salvador Allende, documented via the well-established record of his political career.

detail_orientation.rationale: [NEW_EVIDENCE, Roster32] The Odas Elementales' close attention to everyday objects is now corroborated by a second, physically verifiable independent instance: his Isla Negra house, built and expanded from the late 1930s through the 1950s, contains an entire dedicated room ('Bajo el mar') housing an extensive, thematically organized shell and marine-curio collection (including ships in bottles, figureheads, and a narwhal tusk), with the house's whole nautical architecture -- low ceilings, narrow passageways, an anchor mooring it to the land -- built specifically around this collecting practice rather than the collection being incidental decoration.

planning_orientation.rationale: Canto General's sweeping, multi-book historical scope covering the whole of Latin American history required extensive advance structural planning, documented via the work's own comprehensive organized structure.

independent_thinking.rationale: Joined the Communist Party and sustained an openly declared political position that directly led to his forced exile, a genuinely independent and consequential political stance for a prominent public literary figure of his era.

persistence.rationale: Continued both his poetic and political careers across forced exile and subsequent return, documented via the well-established sustained record of his post-exile output and political re-engagement.

deep_focus.rationale: Sustained an unusually large body of published poetry alongside a demanding diplomatic career, evidencing real sustained concentrated creative effort.

aesthetic_sensitivity.rationale: [NEW_EVIDENCE, Roster32] Wrote consistently in green ink throughout his working life, a specific, sustained, self-explained aesthetic choice -- he described green as the color of hope -- corroborated across multiple independent accounts of his manuscripts and working habits, distinct from an incidental or unremarked preference.

provenance.notes: Third-batch diversity pick: 20th_century, latin_america, literature/diplomacy dual-domain profile. His later, well-documented controversial personal conduct (a confession in his own posthumous memoir describing an assault, and other troubling episodes toward women, publicly re-examined and debated in recent years) was deliberately NOT used to infer any trait score here — per this project's safety rules, this project scores documented behavior relevant to the 34-trait taxonomy, not moral judgment, and inferring personality traits from that specific conduct would risk exactly the kind of character diagnosis this project's rubric prohibits; it is noted here for the record, not silently omitted, but no row above draws on it. Roster32 (2026-09): nearest-to-eligible candidate in the cycle, deliberately deepened rather than expanded -- research targeted genuinely NEW_EVIDENCE, independently-corroborating, for EXISTING rows (not new rows for their own sake), and specifically avoided his political/diplomatic career as FURTHER evidentiary basis, since several PRE-EXISTING rows already legitimately rest on it (his 1948 Senate denunciation of González Videla, the resulting exile and Andes escape, his Communist Party membership and presidential pre-candidacy) -- this is not a defect: this cycle's zero-politics rule governs a person's PRIMARY product identity (his is unambiguously 'poet,' via a Nobel Prize in Literature and global readership), not the absence of any political fact from an individual's documented biography, and those pre-existing rows are not sanitized or removed. All 3 Roster32 changes (2 upgrades, 1 new row) are grounded instead in craft/personal-habit material (a joint improvised speech with Lorca, his shell-collecting/house-building, his green-ink writing ritual), diversifying the evidentiary base rather than replacing what was already there. Same safety exclusion reaffirmed and untouched. 2026-09-12: publication review (eligibility-blind, per docs/checkpoints/profile-publication-vs-match-eligibility.md) found no identity/attribution/provenance defect across all 21 rows -- richest, most complete profile in the cohort, sourced across his own memoir, the Nobel citation, and 3 institutional/press outlets; the excluded assault confession remains excluded, not laundered. Promoted to evidence_approved; publication is independent of eligibility_v2. Eligibility diagnostic (informational only, not a publication factor): post-lock recompute corrects the prior cycle's own diagnosis of what's binding -- the prior holdReason cited 'avgConf 0.515 vs 0.55,' which is the legacy flat average (eligibility_v1-style), not the eligibility_v2 admission statistic; highConfidenceAverage was already 0.63 pre-cycle (comfortably passing), and the real binding constraint was always highConfidenceCount (8 of 12 required). This cycle's new evidence honestly moved the count from 8 to 10 (detail_orientation crossed the 0.5 line; the new aesthetic_sensitivity row landed exactly at 0.5) -- scored=21, coverage=0.63, highConfCount=10 (need 12), highConfAvg=0.62. Two short of match-eligible. Per this cycle's explicit rule against hunting one more trait once a result is known, no further research was attempted after this number became visible.
